section: common mistakes and misconceptions
text: Common mistakes and misconceptions "Muon replaces AdamW everywhere." It handles 2D hidden-layer matrices only; embeddings, the output head and norm gains stay on AdamW. "Muon makes the update exactly orthogonal." Five tuned Newton-Schulz steps leave singular values spread around 1 (roughly 0.7 to 1.2 in practice, inside Jordan's 0.7 to 1.3 target), by design. "QK-Clip clips logits." It rescales weights after the step; that step's forward and backward passes are unchanged, and a logit soft-cap is the method that clips logits. "QK-Clip permanently constrains K2." It fired only in the first 70,000 steps, on 12.7% of heads, and never afterwards. "KDA is pure linear attention." Kimi Linear and K3 are hybrids; one layer in four (24 of 93 in K3) is full MLA, and that is where exact recall lives. "Per-channel gating is the same as GDN." GDN forgets with one rate per head; KDA has one rate per key channel. "A linear-attention layer always uses less memory than a cache." Its state is fixed, not small: a K3 KDA layer holds 1,572,864 numbers per request, as much as an MLA layer's cache at about 2,700 tokens.
label: depth

section: common mistakes and misconceptions
text: The saving appears only at long context. "Expert sparsity and the total over active ratio are the same number." K2 is 48 by experts and 31.9 by parameters; K3 is 56 and 26.9, so they rank the two models in opposite orders. "Attention Residuals are cross-attention to earlier layers' tokens." They mix whole earlier layer outputs for the same token, with weights set by one learned vector per layer; no token attends to another through them. "The 4-bit checkpoint is a community quantisation." The 4-bit weights are the trained release format. "K3's checkpoint is all 4-bit." Only the routed experts are MXFP4; the other 57 billion parameters stay in higher precision, which is why the checkpoint is 1.56 TB rather than 1.49 TB. "K3 is modified MIT like K2." K3 has its own Kimi K3 License with an extra commercial threshold for Model-as-a-Service businesses.
